newsitem.title: UK: Greek, Turkish leaders agree Cyprus meetings plan.
newsitem.headline: Greek, Turkish leaders agree Cyprus meetings plan.

text.p: The two leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities have agreed to hold occasional meetings on the island to discuss humanitarian issues, Greek Cypriot President Glafcos Clerides said on Tuesday.
Speaking in London after a meeting with British Prime Minister Tony Blair, he told reporters he could not as yet detail the subjects to be discussed with Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash.
"We will discuss that when we get back to Cyprus," he said.
British diplomatic sources said the decision to hold meetings was taken during four days of United Nations sponsored talks between Clerides and Denktash at Troutbeck near New York last week.
Clerides was visiting London on his way home from the meeting, his first contact with Denktash for three years, and their first negotiations for five.
Further discussions on the constitutional future of the divided island are due to take place in Switzerland from August 11 to 16.
The sources said they hoped the first meeting on humanitarian issues would be held before that.

Topics might include tackling forest fires which spread across the island's Greek-Turkish dividing line and identifying the whereabouts of people missing since the 1974 Turkish occupation of Northern Cyprus.

Diplomats hope that once elections for the Greek Cypriot presidency have taken place next February, a further round of U.N. sponsored talks will be held in an attempt to get agreement on a federal constitution for the divided island.
Such a constitution would provide for a bizonal federal state in which the Greek Cypriots, who at present occupy 63 percent of the divided island, would gain extra land, the sources said.
